The problem

AI agents can spend money while nobody is watching.

One bad loop, one expensive model, or one forgotten customer workflow can turn into a surprise bill. Forsig gives each agent a budget boundary before it reaches OpenAI.

Runaway loop

Block before spend

Forsig estimates token cost and rejects requests that would cross daily, monthly, or per-request limits.

Wrong model

Keep models under policy

Allow cheap models for routine work and block expensive or unapproved models before they run.

No visibility

See every request

Track status, model, token counts, estimated cost, actual usage, latency, and block reason.

Emergency

Pause instantly

Stop a risky agent with one kill switch while you inspect logs and fix the underlying workflow.

60 second product story

From blind provider calls to controlled agent traffic.

Developers should understand Forsig before reading a single feature list: your agent asks, Forsig checks policy, then the provider call is allowed or blocked.

Before Agents call OpenAI directly

No per-agent budgets, weak customer-level visibility, and no fast way to stop a bad loop.

After Agents pass through Forsig

Every request is checked, priced, logged, and blocked or allowed according to your policy.

Developer speed

Add budget protection without rewriting your agent.

Use raw OpenAI-compatible base URL for the fastest path, then add SDK headers when you want session, customer, and instance tracking.

JavaScript
import OpenAI from "openai";
import { forsigHeaders, newForsigSession } from "@forsig/sdk";

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.FORSIG_API_KEY,
  baseURL: "https://gateway.forsig.com/v1",
});

await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-4o-mini",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello" }],
}, {
  headers: forsigHeaders({
    sessionId: newForsigSession(),
    externalUserId: "user_123",
  }),
});
Python
from openai import OpenAI
from forsig import forsig_headers, new_forsig_session

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["FORSIG_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://gateway.forsig.com/v1",
)

client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    extra_headers=forsig_headers(
        session_id=new_forsig_session(),
        external_user_id="user_123",
    ),
)
How it works

Four steps from exposed agent to protected traffic.

01

Store provider key

Add your OpenAI key once. Forsig encrypts it and issues agent-scoped virtual keys.

02

Register agent

Name the external agent, choose model policy, set spend limits, and record required instructions.

03

Route requests

Use the OpenAI-compatible base URL or SDK helpers to attach session/user metadata.

04

Block or pause

Stop expensive loops, disallowed models, budget breaches, or the whole agent instantly.

FAQ

Questions founders and developers ask first.

Does Forsig store my OpenAI API key?

Yes. The MVP stores provider keys encrypted, never displays them after creation, and uses Forsig virtual keys in your app.

Do I have to use the SDK?

No. The SDK is optional. You can use any OpenAI-compatible client by changing the base URL and API key.

Does Forsig replace my agent framework?

No. Forsig registers and controls your external agents. Your agent code remains in your app.

Will Forsig store prompts?

Not by default. The MVP stores metadata, token counts, costs, prompt hashes, policy outcomes, and block reasons.
